## Why visit

A particularly useful addition for two beer enthusiasts because it offers an actual brewery experience as well as a traditional pub visit. The oak-beamed inn houses a microbrewery below the bar, producing beer served upstairs; the operator advertises guided cellar tours followed by tasting. Its food offer allows the visit to become a longer lunch or dinner stop. Pair it with the Brewery Tap to compare two quite different historic settings, or with That Beer Place for cider afterwards. Give the production visit priority only after arranging an available date directly.

## Beer

Official brewery page confirms onsite cask and keg production across bitters, pales, IPA, red ales and porter; CAMRA documents hand-pulled house beers.

## Plan the visit

The operator offers a roughly 45-minute tour plus tasting and sells a two-adult voucher. A voucher is not a confirmed November slot: arrange directly. Cellar stairs and standing are involved.

**Getting there:** Northgate Street within Chester’s city centre; combine with the other central Chester venues.

Check [November transport issues](../logistics.md) for date-specific disruption.
